chunks: 3309 - And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudhayl, from Abu al-Hasan, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked him about the testimony of women: is it valid in marriage, divorce, or stoning?

He said: The testimony of women is accepted in matters that men are not able to look at. It is accepted in marriage if there is a man with them. It is not accepted in divorce nor in blood cases. It is accepted in the hadd of zina when there are three men and two women, and the testimony of two men and four women is not accepted.

key_terms.الدَّمِ: blood cases, meaning cases involving unlawful killing or bodily harm
key_terms.النِّسَاءِ: women whose testimony is being discussed in legal cases
key_terms.حَدِّ الزِّنَا: the prescribed legal punishment concerning zina

ai.seo_question: In which legal cases is the testimony of women accepted in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning when the testimony of women is accepted in judicial matters. It distinguishes between cases such as marriage, divorce, blood cases, and zina, specifying the combinations of witnesses that are legally valid.
